thread:
Taylor (Procurement): FYI: QuotaSage sent revised terms for the renewal. They added a "usage smoothing" clause and an "anchoring_credit" line. I want to run a counter before we lock pilot. Thoughts?

Sam (Finance): Can you paste the smoothing clause? I'm worried about retroactive price moves.

Taylor (Procurement): Quote text copy: `Usage smoothing: provider may apply smoothing adjustments up to 15% of billed usage in months 2-4 to align with committed baseline.` Also: `anchoring_credit = max( min(0.15*commit, 40000), 0 ) applied at contract start and reconciled quarterly.` PDF link: https://qsage.example.com/quote/RED-2026-v2.pdf

Jo (Eng-ML): :grimacing: "smoothing adjustments" sounds like they can rewrite our bill later. We have bursty inference; those months matter. Ask them to remove smoothing for pilot months.

Nina (Legal): Add: No retrospective billing changes after invoice finalization. Any reconciliations must be prospective and require 30 days' notice. Also want explicit meter definition and CSV export daily.

billing-bot: Draft estimate created: QS-2026-EST, projected monthly cost $32,400 at commit level. https://billing.redwood/estimates/QS-2026-EST

Sam (Finance): Request: replace percent smoothing with absolute $ cap per month. Percent of usage is hard to forecast and penalizes growth.

Taylor (Procurement): Proposed counter bullets I'm thinking to send: 1) Delete smoothing for pilot months 1-3; 2) Cap any adjustment to $10k/month and never retroactive; 3) Define token = user-visible generation token; embeddings billed separately at EMB rate or excluded for pilot; 4) KV cache ingress/egress excluded from ingest GB; 5) Monthly CSV (daily rows) + API endpoint for usage; 6) Anchoring credit to vest over 3 months and refundable if we terminate for convenience; 7) Provide sample billing calc for 50/100/200% of commit.

Jo (Eng-ML): Add: confirm whether quantization requirement is performance suggestion or contract requirement. If they mandate quantization, need to know supported precisions and latency SLOs.

Sam (Finance): Also ask for a line item showing network/egress vs compute vs model charges. We need to map to our cost centers.

Nina (Legal): I'll add: 60-day dispute window, no unilateral retro price increases mid-term, audit right once per year with 30 days' notice.

Taylor (Procurement): Good. I'll craft an email with those points. Any preferred wording for the refundable anchor?

Sam (Finance): "Anchoring credit will be applied monthly as a bill credit and will be refunded pro-rata within 30 days upon termination for convenience during the pilot period."

Jo (Eng-ML): If they push on anchor size, propose scaling: 10% of commit for pilot, escalates on renewal.

Taylor (Procurement): Cool. I'll post a draft in #vendors-review later today. If vendor replies with retroactive recalc language, we walk away or ask for escrowed credits.

Nina (Legal): Loop me in on vendor email. I'll redline SLA and termination clauses in parallel.

Taylor (Procurement): Thanks. /cc @billing-bot for updated estimate after counter.

billing-bot: Noted. Will recalc estimate once counter accepted.

Jo (Eng-ML): Standing by to review the vendor's technical annex.

Taylor (Procurement): Draft posted: https://docs.redwood/internal/vendors/qsage-counter-1742509876.md — please comment before 3pm PT.
